structure: ICH M15 Appendix 2, Model Analysis Report: Executive Summary, Introduction, Objectives, Data and Methods, Results, Discussion, Conclusions, Appendices (EMA/CHMP/ICH/496426/2024, 9 February 2026, page 16-17).

sections.executive_summary: The platform implements the published lenalidomide population pharmacokinetic model of Hughes et al. (2019) at its typical values, with creatinine clearance (Cockcroft-Gault) and fat-free mass as covariates, to draw exposure curves for synthetic profiles. Three locked checks compared it with group data from outside its source: the dedicated renal study (CC-5013-PK-001), the same study with virtual subjects matched to its demographics, and myeloma patients on reduced doses (Bridoux 2016, prespecified, with its outcome largely known from the abstract). Mild impairment is consistent throughout; moderate and severe impairment are under-predicted in both studies. The model is shown for research and education with those bands flagged.
sections.introduction: Hughes et al. (2019) published a population model of lenalidomide in which apparent clearance falls with creatinine clearance and scales with fat-free mass. The platform uses it for typical-value exposure curves in the Patient Lab and in comparisons with Kim 2026. The paper does not state which body weight its Cockcroft-Gault calculation used; the platform assumes ideal body weight and shows the alternatives as sensitivity cases, and the question is open with the authors. The main-text parameters, the between-patient variability and the structure were transcribed from the article and its supplementary control stream, and an AI review on 10 November 2026 found them to match; no source data or run outputs were available to reproduce the fit.
objectives: Reproduce the published typical-value model for synthetic profiles, with its covariates and stated variability.
Test, under plans locked before computation, whether its kidney-function effect reproduces group exposure in a dedicated renal study and in myeloma patients outside its source data.
Record which kidney-function bands the model may be shown for without a warning.
discussion: Mild impairment is consistent in every check and scenario. Moderate and severe impairment are under-predicted in CC-5013-PK-001, unchanged when the virtual subjects were matched to that study's demographics, and again in myeloma patients (Bridoux 2016), so the non-cancer population of the renal study does not explain the gap.

The Bridoux check was prespecified before the per-group values were seen, but it was not a strong test: the abstract stated that exposure stayed within ±25% of target on label doses, which already implied the moderate ratio, and part of the study's results text (the relative AUC24 values, which give the primary endpoint once multiplied by the known dose ratios) was seen while locating its design table, before the observed file was committed. For Hughes the outcome was effectively known before the article was opened.

The checks compare group means only, with 5 to 7 subjects per group in CC-5013-PK-001. The weight basis of Cockcroft-Gault in the source remains unresolved; it changes the computed clearance most in heavier people. Random effects are set to zero for the typical curve.
conclusions: The model is consistent with outside data in mild kidney impairment and is shown there without a band warning.
It under-predicts exposure in moderate and severe impairment in two independent studies; those bands are flagged on every page that shows them.
Further checking needs unseen data, and an answer from the authors on the weight basis.

not_this: Not a regulatory submission and not an independent assessment of the published model. It documents how the platform implemented and checked the model. Generated from the platform's pinned plans and reports; the narrative sections were written by the AI assistant and have not been reviewed independently.
